paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when God says He has delivered something into your hand, it is DONE. He told Moses, "See, I have delivered into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land." (Deuteronomy 2:24) Then He told Moses about Og, "Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand…" (Deuteronomy 3:2) The promise came first, and the battle only showed it was true.

Now look at how Moses went about it. He sent an offer of peace first, and he asked only to pass through on the main road and pay in silver (Deuteronomy 2:26-28). Sihon would not let them pass, and Moses says why: "the LORD your God had made his spirit stubborn and his heart obstinate, that He might deliver him into your hand…" (Deuteronomy 2:30). I think that's a heavy thing to read, and Moses doesn't soften it. He just wants Israel to see that God was the One steering the whole thing, not the walls or the armies.

So what do you do with that, baker? When the "Og" in your life shows up at your door, you don't have to fear him, because the One who promised is bigger. Moses says it plainly: "the LORD our God delivered him over to us." (Deuteronomy 2:33) Even the bed of iron at the end of the passage is there to remind you how big the giant was and how much bigger God's word is (Deuteronomy 3:11). Moses is NOT done preaching yet, so keep that promise close and keep the ovens warm.
